notes.meaning: The Teacher observed the terrible cruelty and injustice taking place all across the world. He saw the tears of those being crushed by powerful leaders, yet no one dared to comfort or help them. Earthly power is often abused, leaving the weak feeling helpless when God's eternal justice is left out of view.

Looking only at life in this painful world, the Teacher judged that the dead are better off than the living. People who have already died are free from the cruelty and heavy burdens of earthly oppressors. Death looks like a welcome escape when life is viewed strictly apart from the hope of eternity.

The Teacher added that a person who was never born is even more fortunate than the dead. Someone who never existed has never had to see or feel any of the wickedness and misery done on earth. This shows how deep human despair can become when someone looks only at life under the sun.

Much of the hard work and skilled effort people put into life is driven by rivalry and jealousy toward their neighbors. Success often breeds envy from others instead of the honor a person hoped to receive. Striving to get ahead of everyone else is an empty pursuit that never brings lasting peace.

Some people see the envy caused by hard work and swing to the opposite extreme of complete laziness. The foolish person folds his hands, refuses to work, and slowly ruins himself through hunger and poverty. Being idle is not true rest; it is just another form of self-destruction.

Having one handful of goods with peace and quietness is far better than having both hands full of wealth gained through exhausting stress. Chasing after more riches than we need brings constant worry and frustration. A wise person learns moderation and stays content with enough.
The Teacher turned his attention to another empty sight in this life. He watched how greed can make a person waste their entire life in loneliness.

A wealthy man lives completely alone, with no child or brother to share his estate. Even though he has nobody to provide for, he works endlessly and his eyes are never satisfied with his riches. He never stops to ask why he is starving his soul of enjoyment for wealth he cannot keep.

Two people working together accomplish far more than one person laboring alone. Their shared efforts bring a much better reward and make their daily toil worthwhile. God made human beings to live in fellowship, marriage, and friendship rather than cold isolation.

If two friends walk together and one slips, the other is right there to lift him back up. But it is terrible for someone who falls all alone, because there is no one around to help him. Companions protect each other when hard times, physical danger, or spiritual struggles strike.

On cold nights, two people lying down together share their warmth and stay comfortable. A single person sleeping alone has a much harder time staying warm. True companionship provides physical comfort and warms the human heart through shared care.

An attacker can easily defeat a solitary traveler, but two people standing together can resist and defend themselves. A rope made of three twisted strands is even harder to pull apart or break. God gives us partners and friends so we can have safety and strength in numbers.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Many teachers apply the cord of three strands to Christian marriage, explaining that the third strand represents God binding the husband and wife together.

notes.meaning: A poor young man who possesses wisdom is far better off than an aging king who has become foolish and refuses to listen to advice. Long years and royal dignity mean nothing when a ruler grows stubborn and proud. True honor comes from having a teachable heart rather than a crown.

A wise youth can rise all the way from a prison cell or humble poverty to become the ruler of a kingdom. At the same time, an unwise king who was born to royalty can lose everything and become poor. Human positions are unstable, and outward rank is no guarantee of lasting success.

The Teacher watched the whole living generation rush to support the young successor who took the old king's place. Crowds love a new leader and quickly gather around the fresh ruler in hopes of better days. Yet this surge of popular support is only temporary.

Endless crowds of people may celebrate a new king at first, but later generations will eventually turn away and lose interest in him. The praise of the public never lasts very long. Chasing after political popularity and earthly fame is as pointless as trying to chase the wind.
